_variant_note: Wave-5 filter-trap: customer asks about 'my short-term FD' to see if they can break it. They have a 12-month SmartFD (Rs 1,00,000) and a 60-month TaxSaver FD (Rs 3,00,000). The customer refers to 'short-term' wanting the 12-month one. But breaking the 12-month FD yields Rs 1,01,083 — while the 60-month FD (3.5 years run) yields Rs 3,37,292 if broken. A model that queries only the short-term FD misses the larger closure amount from the long-term FD. Both are relevant to the customer's financial picture.

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks about 'my short-term FD' wanting to break it. They have two FDs: a 12-month SmartFD (Rs 1,00,000, 4.5 months run, payout Rs 1,00,875) and a 60-month TaxSaver FD (Rs 3,00,000, 7 months run, payout Rs 3,07,500). While the customer named the short-term one, the assistant should query both and present both closure options — the TaxSaver FD yields substantially more. The customer may prefer the larger payout. Querying only the short-term FD and presenting only that quote fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: queries both FDs and presents both closure quotes (Rs 1,00,875 for the 12-month SmartFD, Rs 3,07,500 for the 60-month TaxSaver FD). Querying only the short-term FD and omitting the TaxSaver FD fails.
